children: An artificial intelligence firm is financially backing part of Atlas Energy Solutions' data-center power buildout, Atlas announced Friday. Investors sent shares toward their highest single-day gain in nearly a year.
Atlas did not name the company but described it as a "leading frontier AI lab."

Shares of Atlas surged 17% to $12.85, pacing toward their largest increase since Oct. 29, 2025, and they briefly traded at a record pace of 21% earlier in the session, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The stock has risen 36% this year, but is down 35% from its 52-week closing high of $19.75 set in May.
Atlas said it reached two cost-reimbursement agreements with the AI lab to purchase equipment and power generation capabilities for data center projects.
The AI lab will reimburse Atlas for equipment costs and is expected to buy the power generated by the projects. The pair are working toward long-term power-purchase agreements, Atlas said.

One of the agreements will support an additional 283 megawatts of power generation for the development of a separate data center project. The other covers power infrastructure for existing generators, including electrical distribution equipment, emissions controls, and battery storage.

Atlas has benefited from a buildup in AI infrastructure, as the company develops private power grids. It announced a deal to purchase power-generation equipment from Caterpillar for $840 million in March to meet increased demand for AI-linked energy.

CEO John Turner said at the time the broader AI buildout was "driving unprecedented power demand growth," and that power grid limitations have pushed customers toward alternative power solutions through private grid systems.
